chunks: A prohibition was issued against visiting the graves of Quraysh and al-Ha'ir. Then, after some months, the vizier called al-Baqta'i and said to him: “Meet the Banu al-Furat and the Bursiyyin, and tell them not to visit the graves of Quraysh, for the caliph has ordered that everyone who visits be checked and seized.”

key_terms.الْحَيْرِ: al-Ha'ir, the sacred area associated with Karbala
key_terms.الْخَلِيفَةُ: the caliph, the ruling political authority
key_terms.زِيَارَةِ: visitation, especially to graves or sacred sites
key_terms.فَيُقْبَضَ عَلَيْهِ: that he be arrested or seized
key_terms.مَقَابِرِ قُرَيْشٍ: the graves of Quraysh, referring to a known burial site

ai.seo_question: Why was visitation to the graves of Quraysh and al-Ha'ir temporarily prohibited in this report?
ai.summary: This report describes a period in which visiting the graves of Quraysh and al-Ha'ir was outwardly prohibited due to political surveillance and danger. It reflects the pressures imposed by the ruling authority and preserves a historical moment connected to the circumstances of the Shi'a community.

en.hubeali: ‘A prohibition order came out (from the 12<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) from visiting the graves of the Qureysh and Al-Ha’ir. So when it was after a few months, the Vizier called Al-Baqtai’y and said to him, ‘Meet up with the Clan of Al-Furat and Al-Bursiyyeen and say to them, ‘You should not be visiting the graves of the Qureysh for it is the order of the Caliph that he would inspect everyone who visits and be arrested over it’.
en.sarwar: 31. Ali ibn Muhammad has said the following.

“A prohibition to visit the Quryash cemetery and al-Hira (Karbala) came out of the holy location (office of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.). After a few months the Vizier (abu al-Fath Ja‘far ibn Furat) summoned al-Baqtia, and said to him, “Meet the clan of bnu Furat and al-Bursiyin and tell them not to visit Quraysh cemetery because the Caliph has decide to see all those who would visit these places be arrested.”
